items.fullText: 삼성, 샘 올트먼과 ‘AI 혁신’ 간담회 개최 ‘AI Driven’ 경영 강화… 전사적 AX 추진 가속 2026/10/31 AUDIO Play Download 공유 레이어 열기 인쇄하기 삼성, 샘 올트먼 CEO 초청해 AI 시대 미래 경영 전략 논의 삼성은 31일 경기도 용인 삼성인력개발원에서 삼성전자 등 주요 관계사 사장단을 대상으로 샘 올트먼(Sam Altman) OpenAI CEO 초청 간담회를 개최했다. 이날 간담회에는 전자·금융·바이오 등 삼성 관계사 사장단 50여 명이 참석했으며, 샘 올트먼 CEO와 함께 ‘AI가 바꿀 다음 10년, 기업의 선택’을 주제로 진행됐다. 삼성 사장단과 샘 올트먼 CEO는 AI 기술의 발전 방향과 활용 가능성을 살펴보고, 이를 바탕으로 새롭게 형성될 시장과 사업 기회에 대한 의견을 나눴다. 또한 AI가 기업의 의사결정과 조직 운영에 미칠 영향을 짚어보며, 새로운 경영 환경에서 경영진이 갖춰야 할 역량에 대해서도 소통했다. 삼성은 전사적 AX 추진을 위한 사장단 교육의 일환으로 경영진의 AI 이해도를 높이고 미래 경영 전략을 모색하기 위해 이번 간담회를 마련했다. 삼성은 글로벌 AI 혁신을 주도하는 OpenAI의 CEO를 초청하는 등 AI 시대의 변화에 선제적으로 대응하고 미래 경쟁력을 강화하는 데 힘을 쏟고 있다. AI 시대의 경쟁력이 경영진의 판단력과 실행력에서 비롯된다는 인식 아래, 사장단이 앞장서 AI를 배우고 활용하는 문화를 확산시키고 있다. 삼성전자와 OpenAI는 지난해 10월 글로벌 AI 인프라 구축을 위한 협력 의향서(LOI)를 체결하고, OpenAI의 스타게이트 프로젝트에 필요한 메모리 반도체 공급을 추진해 왔다. 당시 삼성SDS는 AI 데이터센터 구축과 기업용 AI 서비스 분야에서 협력하기로 했으며, 삼성물산과 삼성중공업은 해상 부유식 데이터센터 공동 개발을 진행하기로 했다. 올해 7월에는 이재용 삼성전자 회장이 미국 샌프란시스코 OpenAI 본사를 방문하는 등 양사 간 교류도 지속해 왔다. 삼성 사장단, 지난 6월에 이어 생성형 AI 집중교육 추가 진행 삼성 사장단은 이날 샘 올트먼 CEO와의 간담회에 앞서 생성형 AI 실습 교육을 진행했다. 지난 6월 사장단을 대상으로 첫 AI 집중교육을 실시한 데 이어, 4개월 만에 시행된 추가 교육이다. 삼성은 사장단부터 AI 기술을 직접 익히고 업무에 적용할 수 있도록 교육 프로그램을 지속 운영하고 있으며, 이를 실제 활용할 수 있는 능력을 높이는 데 초점을 맞췄다. 사장단은 흩어진 경영 자료를 AI로 정리해 자신만의 ‘지식저장소’를 구성하고, 의사결정에 AI를 활용하는 역량을 높였다. 삼성, ‘AI Driven’ 경영 본격화… 전사적 AI 대전환 추진 삼성은 지난 6월부터 연구개발에서 생산·마케팅·지원 업무까지 전 분야에 AI를 도입하는 ‘AI 대전환’을 본격 추진하고 있다. AI를 활용해 업무 생산성과 사업 경쟁력을 높이고, 제품과 서비스는 물론 기업 운영 전반에 AI를 접목해 나갈 계획이다. 이를 위해 관계사별 사업 특성과 업무 환경에 맞는 AI 활용 방안을 마련하고, 임직원들이 AI를 적극적으로 활용할 수 있는 기반을 확대하고 있다. 지난 6월 사장단 교육을 시작으로 약 2,300명의 임원을 대상으로 교육을 추진했으며, 교육 대상을 일반 직원까지 확대해 2027년 2월까지 전 임직원 대상 AI 교육을 완료한다는 목표를 제시했다. 삼성은 관계사별 AI 전담조직을 구축하고, 외부 생성형 AI 서비스의 업무 활용도 확대하고 있다. items.t: Anthropic expected to receive high ‘junk’ rating from credit agencies following IPO, FT report says
items.d: Blackstone's forecast is just a prediction, but naturally, a high junk rating would make it more difficult and costlier for Anthropic to raise the money to keep funding its massive spending that has undergirded its business.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 2:52 PM PDT · October 30, 2026 Image Credits: Anna Moneymaker / Getty Images Lucas Ropek Anthropic expected to receive high ‘junk’ rating from credit agencies following IPO, FT report says Anthropic is expected to receive a high “junk” rating from credit rating agencies following its initial public offering, according to a report from the Financial Times. The FT says the investment giant Blackstone, the anchor investor in a recent $63 billion deal to finance Anthropic’s chips, told investors in the deal that it expects the AI lab to receive a “high” junk rating after its IPO. Previously, the FT notes, Blackstone had said the opposite: that the Claude maker would receive an investment-grade rating (indicating low risk for lenders) before 2027 rolls around. Now Blackstone expects double B range rating, the top tier of speculative “junk” grade, according to the reporting. TechCrunch reached out to Anthropic and Blackstone but both declined to comment. Blackstone’s forecast is just a prediction, but naturally, a high junk rating would make it more difficult and costlier for Anthropic to raise the money to keep funding its massive spending that has undergirded its business. The lab has been on a spending spree, racking up large compute power deals throughout the past 12 months, which has worried investors . Anthropic officially filed to go public earlier this week, kicking off a wave of speculation about how the massive IPO would impact the broader AI industry . items.t: Last-minute Halloween costumes for tech nerds
items.d: No Halloween costume? Just be a deceptively cute AI agent icon, a PHP vulnerability, or sleepy time Bryan Johnson.
items.fullText: It happens to the best of us — you’ve completely dropped the ball on figuring out a Halloween costume. Naturally, you’ve decided to solve this problem by turning to… TechCrunch? Yeah, sure, why not. I’ve got some ideas. Here are some last-minute techy Halloween costumes. Effort levels vary. Recursive self-improvement AI leaders like Dario Amodei and Sam Altman have expressed their fears that AI is developing too quickly , but if AI models become capable of “recursive self-improvement,” they’ll be able to advance on their own without human intervention, rendering any efforts to “pace the frontier” futile. I’m not sure how to visually represent the idea of an AI building itself, but you could really lean into the “self-improvement” part and forget the “recursive” aspect — it’s a last-minute Halloween costume. You don’t need to try that hard. Dress as the version of yourself you imagine becoming every year when you make New Year’s resolutions. Carry around a self-help or productivity book like “Atomic Habits” or anything by Malcolm Gladwell, a yoga mat, and a huge bottle of water. Leave in the middle of the party to “go to therapy” when you actually just want to go home. Brag to people about how good your Oura Ring’s sleep score is. You are the embodiment of someone trying to better themselves. You are recursive self-improvement. It’s almost Elizabeth Holmes-esque — they look innocent, so you underestimate their potential to cause disaster. items.t: Zest’s new AI agent finds restaurants and books reservations over text
items.d: Can't agree on where to eat? Zest's AI concierge can combine everyone's tastes, put restaurant options to a vote, and make the reservation.
items.fullText: Zest , the restaurant discovery app that launched earlier this year, is already thinking about a future where mobile apps are no longer the primary interface. On Thursday, the startup introduced a new feature: a personal AI-powered “restaurant concierge” that lives in your text messages, similar to other popular AI agents like Instinct or Poke. The launch reflects a broader shift in how startups are thinking about AI, as conversational AI agents take on tasks that had previously required users to launch stand-alone mobile apps. For Zest, that means bringing its restaurant recommendations into texts, then allowing users to immediately take the next step of booking a table. “The agent is the product now,” explains Zest founder and CEO Mario Gomez-Hall. “You text it, and it answers from your own history and your friends’. It doesn’t need weeks of conversation to learn you because it starts from where you’ve actually been,” he said. Image Credits: Zest Originally founded in November 2024, with $1.8 million in pre-seed backing from Alexis Ohanian at 776 and Steve Jang at Kindred Ventures, the app’s unique feature is that it links up with users’ credit cards to track where they’re actually eating out to get a sense of their tastes and interests. With this data on hand, Zest can make tailored suggestions of what places you might like to try next, whether that’s in your own city or suggestions of places to try when you’re traveling. The credit card data used by Zest’s app is imported via the financial services company Plaid , which is used by banks and other fintech and budgeting apps. Zest says it focuses only on those transactions in the food and drink categories when making its personalized map and lists. items.d: While science fiction lore tells us that humans will meet extraterrestrial life in the form of little green men, the detail that should raise hairs this Halloween is this: the search for extraterrestrial intelligence took a major leap forward with AI, and it increasingly focuses on AI agents built by humans listening for AI agents […]
items.fullText: Things That Go Beep in the Night: Agentic AI Joins the Search for Extraterrestrial Signals Scientists at the Allen Telescope Array have integrated the NVIDIA Holoscan platform to search for signals that may come from aliens — or the AI they built. October 30, 2026 by Chris Porter 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! While science fiction lore tells us that humans will meet extraterrestrial life in the form of little green men, the detail that should raise hairs this Halloween is this: the search for extraterrestrial intelligence took a major leap forward with AI, and it increasingly focuses on AI agents built by humans listening for AI agents built by aliens. Some scientists have suggested that extraterrestrial civilizations, if they exist, could be billions of years older than humanity. Such civilizations might have developed technologies far beyond humanity’s, including forms of AI. Breakthrough Listen and the SETI Institute are bringing agentic AI into the daily search for extraterrestrial intelligence. At the Allen Telescope Array in Northern California, agents can now steer the instrument, enhance and correct incoming data, and apply AI models to the incoming stream — all from a single natural language request. The NVIDIA Holoscan platform processes the massive streams of sensor data, giving agents live data to act on. The result is a faster, more adaptable search for potential signals from extraterrestrial life and technologies. “As our new agentic observatories reach out into the universe, what they find may have much more in common with themselves than with the humans who created them,” said Andrew Siemion, Bernard M. Oliver chair for SETI at the SETI Institute and principal investigator of Breakthrough Listen. “But this isn’t something to fear. items.t: DoorDash said it’s only received ‘several hundred’ orders from AI agents
items.d: DoorDash said that it is open to working with third-party agent makers.
items.fullText: There’s a big uproar about AI agents taking over commerce and orders, but that might not be the case just yet. Delivery company DoorDash revealed during its third-quarter earnings call that it has only seen “several hundred” orders from third-party agents like Muse, Instinct, Fo, and others. For comparison, the company said in its 2025 report it completes an average of 3 million deliveries daily. “I would say that this [using agents to order] is something that is still a very dynamic area. And my take on all things technology is you never want to fight gravity. But at the same time, you don’t want to be delusional,” DoorDash CEO Tony Xu said in an answer to an analyst’s questions about the topic. “What I mean by that is if you look at where AI agents are today, we’re seeing maybe several hundred orders in total from some of these third-party agents,” he said. Xu mentioned that users are still predominantly placing orders through DoorDash’s app. However, the company wants to learn more about agentic use cases and develop a healthy relationship with third-party agent makers. He added that, in the future, there could be an opportunity for it to advertise within these agents. DoorDash has its own agents, including a text-to-order agent it launched in September , a CLI agent introduced in July , and a chatbot called Ask DoorDash it launched in June, which allows users to place orders through prompts and photos . The company also released an MCP to enable ordering from other chatbots for corporate ordering. The space of agent-based ordering is evolving, as websites are still deciding whether to allow them to access their content or not. Amazon has been blocking such personal agents, but Walmart has laid out a red carpet for them in order to snag some business from its competitors . items.fullText: Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations With Frontier AI Agents See how developers are combining AI agents with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to build simulation applications, test physical behavior and guide improvements. October 29, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Your browser doesn't support HTML5 video. Here is a link to the video instead. Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. Developers are combining frontier AI models with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to help carry out that work — building applications for exploring scenarios, investigating failures and improving designs. Developers direct AI agents through natural-language instructions, review results and guide changes. Omniverse libraries provide GPU-accelerated physics, rendering and sensor simulation capabilities. Explore the projects below to see frontier AI models such as GPT-6 Astra at work, and check back for new examples from NVIDIA teams and developers across the ecosystem. Create an Editable Building Model From Site Scans 🔗 https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/relay-video-v14-1080p.mp4 Planning warehouse automation requires a model of the building itself, but shelving and machinery can obscure its structure in site scans. Omniverse brings together real-to-sim tools and agent skills to help developers turn real-world captures into editable starting environments for physical AI simulation. David Wehr, from NVIDIA’s simulation technology team, built on that work using Astra to develop a workflow for digitally reconstructing a building without its contents. The goal is an editable, simulation-ready building model where developers can add or reposition shelving and machinery to evaluate warehouse layouts and automation plans before making physical changes. items.fullText: NVIDIA Transforms European Retail, From Digital Discovery to Physical Operations October 21, 2026 by Mavi Nafria 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! European retailers are using open models and physical intelligence across use cases — from a commerce platform cutting inference costs by 90% to to a fulfillment center where collaboration of different robotic fleets is simulated inside a digital twin. Frontier Results With Open Models Retail leaders and technology companies across Europe are using NVIDIA-accelerated open and frontier models to advance agentic commerce, digital product discovery and retail R&D. Shopify post-trains open models to reach frontier-level accuracy at a fraction of the cost. Its engineers use the NVIDIA Megatron Bridge library for faster fine-tuning and NVIDIA NeMo RL for reinforcement learning. Shopify has post-trained NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for the GraphQL subagent integrated into Sidekick, Shopify’s AI assistant for merchants. The subagent retrieves store data for several Sidekick features, including Sidekick Pulse, which researches a merchant’s store and recommends ways to improve it. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements On Shopify’s internal benchmark, the post-trained model surpasses a leading frontier model in accuracy while cutting serving costs by 90% and delivering responses 7x faster. Beyond Sidekick, NVIDIA CCluster vLLM inference optimization software helped Shopify achieve 4.5x faster performance and up to 12x lower inference cost across five additional use cases: catalog enrichment, merchant assistant, e-commerce shopping simulation, product taxonomy classification, and merchant and buyer recommendations. Zooplus , Europe’s leading online pet retailer, with Infosys and NVIDIA technologies rebuilt its product discovery stack for the agentic era. items.fullText: NVIDIA Cloud Partners Scale Across Europe — Sovereign, Open and Built for Safe AI Agents Growing ecosystem of AI clouds across Europe, Nordics, Africa and Central Asia build full-stack NVIDIA DSX Vera Rubin AI factories as AI-native companies drive demand for sovereign compute, training, inference and post-training services. October 21, 2026 by Stuart Pitts 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Demand from AI-natives is pulling the European AI cloud ecosystem forward faster than ever. Developers need compute closer to their data, open models they can customize and serve at scale, and full-stack infrastructure that is secure by design. NVIDIA Cloud Partners across Europe, the Nordics, Africa, and Central Asia are expanding regional compute capacity for model training and inference, helping developers build agentic and physical AI applications, and establishing boundaries around what agents can access and do. Together, they’re turning Europe’s energy, data, research and industrial expertise into productive intelligence — supporting new models, applications, organizations and jobs while giving people more control over where and how they develop and deploy AI. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Sovereign: AI Clouds Building European AI Infrastructure Europe is home to world-class research, engineering talent, industrial expertise, data, the next generation of models and applications that requires large-scale computing close to where that knowledge resides. Regional AI clouds provide the infrastructure foundation on which model builders, enterprises and entire industries can grow. As AI factories scale, power becomes a constraint which makes it critical for every watt to produce more intelligence. Nscale is using the NVIDIA DSX Platform to coordinate power allocation with workload requirements.
